events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This case is filed as a safety dispute. The rider's complaint alleges that during the trip the driver repeatedly commented on her body and asked for her number, and that she felt harassed and unsafe [F3][F4]. That is an allegation of unwanted personal advances / harassment made inside the vehicle [SAFE-1]. Under SAFE-1, where such an allegation appears in the complaint, no automatic adjudication is made and the case goes to a human with a factual summary; the policy execution trace records this element as settled (✓ SAFE-1, allowed outcome escalate only) [SAFE-1].

Reading every message and statement in the record: there are no in-app chat messages at all [F3], and the only text from the driver is his post-trip statement "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened." [F4]. I find no threat, intimidation, sexual remark, hostile or abusive language in any recorded text [F4]. The safety concern in this case therefore does not arise from the recorded words; it arises from the rider's first-person complaint of body comments and a request for her number, of which nothing in the record is a contemporaneous or verbatim account [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. Because the clause is engaged by the nature of the allegation and asks a person, not the system, to read what was said, I do not decide the allegation at all [SAFE-1].

The cabin conduct is not recorded anywhere: the chat slice is empty [F3] and no system record (gps [F1][F2], fare, traffic) can speak to what was said inside the car [F1][F2][F3]. The rider's account and the driver's denial [F4] stand opposed and neither is corroborated; a statement cannot be weighed against the other statement by any record rule, since there is no system record of the cabin to prefer to either [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The record therefore cannot settle the central element the clause needs read, which is exactly the situation SAFE-1 assigns to a human reviewer [SAFE-1].

No route issue arises: actual distance 17.1 km against an optimal route of 17.2 km (−0.1 km) [F1], so no off-route segment exists and no RD-2 computation is available or sought [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2]. No cancellation or waiting fee is in issue, so NS-0/NS-1/NS-6 never enter [F1][F2][NS-1][NS-6]. The fare of $35.70 is the RydeX fixed quote and no fare fact exists to show any unpublished addition, so no monetary relief is computable [F1][FARE-1]. Accordingly the amount is null and the outcome is escalate [SAFE-1].

Profile facts are not used to decide the case: the driver's 327 days, 999 trips in 90 days and 0 upheld disputes [F6] and the rider's clean record [F5] cannot alone determine the safety allegation, and there is no finding against the driver that would engage RD-6 or an account flag [RD-6].

Summary for the human reviewer: (1) what happened — a RydeX night trip, Woodlands Civic Centre → Punggol Waterway Point, pickup 22:29, drop-off 22:54, 17.1 km driven against a 17.2 km optimal route [F1][F2]; (2) the dispute — the rider alleges the driver commented on her body and asked for her number and that she felt harassed and unsafe, while the driver's only record account is "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened." [F4]; (3) what to check — there are no chat messages [F3], so the reviewer should obtain the rider's full written account (timing, wording, whether she used any reporting channel) and the driver's account, note that no system record covers the cabin [F1][F2][F3], and confirm neither account is to be recorded as established fact. If the reviewer finds the alleged words amount to unwanted advances, the SAFE-1 conduct standard applies [SAFE-1]. No route, fare or no-show adjustment is proposed [F1][FARE-1][NS-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP human safety review; place both accounts' statements side by side, do not record either as established fact, and keep the trip fare unchanged pending the review.

actions.detail: Safety dispute type (rider alleges body comments and a request for her number, feeling harassed and unsafe) engaged by SAFE-1, and the record contains no contemporaneous or verbatim account of the words used — empty chat [F3], no cabin system record [F1][F2], and only the driver's post-trip denial [F4]; the case is routed to a human reviewer with the factual summary in the reasoning.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint states that during the trip the driver repeatedly commented on her body and asked for her number, and that she felt harassed and unsafe; this is an allegation of harassment / unwanted personal advances made inside the vehicle.

The chat record contains no in-app messages at all (F3), so the conduct alleged is not recorded in the chat; the only response on the record is the driver's own written statement 'I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened.' (F4), which is a bare denial by the person accused and cannot rebut the rider's account.

The record cannot resolve the conflicting accounts: the rider's allegation of harassment is user-submitted, the driver's denial is likewise only a statement (F4), and no system record (gps F1/F2, fare, traffic) speaks to what was said in the cabin, so this is not a case for automated adjudication and must go to a human.

The ride was a late-night trip (pickup 22:29, drop-off 22:54) with the rider alone in the car, which is the context in which the rider says she felt unsafe; the safety screening in SAFE-1 applies to every case and does not require a trigger word to be present in the record.

No route, fare or no-show issue arises on the system records: actual distance was 17.1 km against a 17.2 km optimal route (F1), so no refund of fare is sought and the only relief requested is human review of the safety complaint.

weaknesses: The allegation rests entirely on the rider's own complaint: the chat record is empty (F3) and there is no audio, GPS or fare fact (F1, F2) that evidences the comments on her body or the request for her number, so the judge may find the factual basis unproven.

The only contradicting material is the driver's written denial 'I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened.' (F4); although a statement cannot outweigh a system record, here there is no system record of the cabin at all, so F4 stands unrebutted on the record.

The driver's profile is clean — 327 days, 999 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F6) — and the rider's profile shows no prior safety or other disputes (F5), so nothing on the profile corroborates or corroborates against the account.

No hint word is present in any recorded text, so the judge may read the threshold in SAFE-1 narrowly; the rider's remedy then rests on the escalation/precautionary purpose of the clause rather than on a provable breach.

claims.assertion: The complaint is an allegation of harassment: the rider says the driver "kept making comments about my body and asked for my number" and that she "felt harassed and unsafe". A harassment allegation of this kind is a SAFE-1 matter and must be screened by a person, not auto-decided; the driver does not concede it and asks that the case be escalated for human review of the words actually used.

The chat record is empty (F3: "No in-app chat messages between rider and driver"), so the only account in the record from the driver's side is F4: "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened." There is no recorded message, no third-party witness and no verbatim quotation of any comment; the rider's complaint is a statement, and on the SAFE-1 screening the record contains nothing that can be verified either way.

The system records are consistent with an ordinary, correctly performed trip: F1 shows the actual distance 17.1 km against an optimal route of 17.2 km (-0.1 km, -0%), i.e. no deviation and no off-route segment, and F2 shows 25.8 min against an estimate of 23.6 min (+2.2 min), a normal variance for a 22:29-22:54 night trip. Nothing in the GPS record indicates erratic, dangerous or unusual driving.

No traffic, weather or incident record exists for this trip (the traffic slice returns no facts), so there is no record of any event during the journey that would corroborate a feeling of physical danger, and equally no RD-4 justification is at issue because no segment was off-route (F1).

The driver's profile (F6) shows 327 days of account age, 4.67 rating over 999 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes and 0 upheld findings in 90 days, which supports asking that no account flag be imposed on the strength of an unverified single allegation; the rider's profile (F5) shows no dispute history either, so nothing in the profiles decides the complaint.

The fare charged, $35.70, is the RydeX fixed quote (non-metered, see the trip data) and no fare facts exist to suggest any unpublished addition; since F1 shows no excess distance and no off-route segment, no refund of any part of the fare is computable from any fare or GPS fact, so the monetary complaint (if any) cannot be sustained.

This is a safety investigation, not a route or no-show claim, and the record contains no route deviation, no cancellation and no waiting fee, so no RD-2, NS-1 or NS-6 finding can be made against the driver on this record.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is specific and first-person ("asked for my number"), and SAFE-1 requires the judge to read the original words and decide whether they amount to harassment; the driver's denial in F4 is only a statement and, being the driver's own post-trip account, carries no more weight than the rider's account.

The chat record is empty (F3), so there is no contemporaneous record that rebuts the rider's version of what was said in the car; the absence of chat messages cuts both ways, and the other side will argue the rider had no channel to document it during the trip.

F2 shows the trip took 2.2 minutes longer than estimated; the other side may use that to argue the driver was not driving briskly, though F1 shows the distance was actually 0.1 km short of optimal and no off-route segment exists.
F6 shows 0 prior upheld disputes, but profile facts cannot decide the case, and RD-6/G4-type arguments from sustained history are unavailable here because there is no finding against the driver.

points.response: Agreed on the mechanism only: the rider's complaint of body comments and a request for her number is a harassment allegation that belongs to a person under SAFE-1, and escalation is exactly what the rider asks for (C1, C3); the driver gains nothing from D1 because escalation is not an acquittal — it is the outcome the rider requested and the driver does not get the case dismissed.

The emptiness of the chat record (F3) cannot be read as the rider's silence: the rider was a passenger in the moving car and had no reason to type, whereas it is the rider's contemporaneous conduct — raising the complaint about the driver's words — that the record preserves, and the driver's denial (F4) is a self-serving post-trip statement that SAFE-1's reading rule weighs no higher than the rider's own account.

D3 proves nothing about the conduct in issue: a clean distance figure (F1) and a 2.2-minute variance (F2) say only that the car stayed on route; SAFE-1 asks the judge to read what was said, and no gps fact can speak to body comments or a request for a phone number.

The absence of traffic/weather facts is neutral and cannot be used by the driver: the rider's complaint is verbal harassment inside the cabin, not an on-road event, so no traffic record would ever exist for it; RD-4 is irrelevant to this dispute type and cites nothing in the rider's brief.

The rider seeks no money, so D6 answers a claim never made; the fare figure of $35.70 is the fixed RydeX quote and no fare facts exist (fare slice empty), meaning the only live relief is the human safety review the rider requests.
Conceded as to scope: no RD-2 refund and no NS-1/NS-6 fee finding is sought or available, and the rider's brief makes no such claim — the case stands or falls on SAFE-1.

The rider's allegation is a statement and I do not concede it: the only driver-side account in the record is F4 ("I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened."), and the chat record is empty (F3). Both descriptions must go to the human reviewer under SAFE-1, which is exactly what I ask for — the clause screens whether the words used are harassment; it does not convert an unverified statement into a finding.

I agree there is no chat record (F3) and no system record of the cabin; that is precisely why no finding can be made against my client on this record and why the case must be escalated — F4 stands unrebutted only in the sense that it stands opposed to an equally unrecorded account, not as an established fact either way. Neither side's account is corroborated, so no adverse determination of harassment can be entered without a person reading both.

Accepted as to procedure: with no system record of what was said in the cabin, the conflicting accounts cannot be resolved here and escalate is the correct action; I simply note that escalation is not a finding against my client, and F4 must be placed in the summary as the driver's own account, not as a contradicted statement.

The 22:29-22:54 timing in F2 is accurate but proves nothing about what was said, and the empty chat (F3) equally supplies no context in the rider's favour; the trip itself shows no incident — F1 records 17.1 km against a 17.2 km optimal route (no off-route segment) and F2 a 2.2-minute variance, so nothing in the system records indicates erratic or dangerous driving or any event inside the car.

Agreed: F1 shows no excess distance and there is no fare fact supporting any refund, so no monetary relief is at issue; my client's clean record (F6: 327 days, 999 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) supports my request that escalation be made to a person without an account flag.
